<p class="lead-statement">I am an antitrust economist whose research and software translate modern industrial organization models into practical tools for merger review, market definition, and competition policy.</p>

I am a Principal Economist at the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System and previously served as an economist at the Federal Trade Commission and the Department of Justice Antitrust Division. My work develops quantitative frameworks and open-source tools for merger review under uncertainty, including market definition, merger simulation, model choice, efficiencies, and financial structure.

Much of my recent work applies these tools to banking and regulated markets, where merger review combines antitrust economics, institutional detail, and public policy. Over nearly two decades of public service, I have led economic investigations and supported high-profile litigations across sectors including retail banking, semiconductors, health insurance, cinema and radio advertising, airlines, and parking services.

## Selected Contributions

<div class="contribution-list">
  <div>Open-source merger simulation and competition-policy software for researchers, practitioners, and students.</div>
  <div>Research on how model choice, conduct assumptions, efficiencies, and financial structure affect merger predictions.</div>
  <div>Market-definition and screening work for merger review under uncertainty, including banking and regulated-industry applications.</div>
  <div>Public agency experience on major merger investigations and litigations at the Federal Reserve Board, FTC, and DOJ Antitrust Division.</div>
</div>

## Research and Policy Focus

<div class="impact-grid">
<div class="impact-card">
<h3>Merger Review and Competition Policy</h3>
<p>I study how quantitative models can inform merger review across horizontal, vertical, labor/product, financial-structure, and complex-integration settings.</p>
</div>
<div class="impact-card">
<h3>Merger Simulation and Open-Source Tools</h3>
<p>I develop software that makes standard antitrust and trade-policy simulation models available in reproducible, practitioner-facing form.</p>
</div>
<div class="impact-card">
<h3>Market Definition and Screening Under Uncertainty</h3>
<p>My work examines how screens, geographic markets, and predicted effects depend on assumptions about conduct, demand, and market boundaries.</p>
</div>
<div class="impact-card">
<h3>Applications to Banking and Regulated Industries</h3>
<p>Recent projects apply merger-review tools to banking and regulated markets, where institutional structure and public policy shape competitive effects.</p>
</div>
</div>
